_meta.description: D6 fixtures for google-antigravity / agent-config. The model reads the tone / expertise / responseLength context entry through the built-in `get_app_context` before every answer (src/agents/agent_config.py). Served through /api/copilotkit-agent-config as agent `agent-config-demo`.
_meta.googleAntigravityStaging: google-antigravity staging: the Antigravity Go harness owns the conversation history and never sends role:"tool" messages, so hasToolResult/toolCallId never fire and every leg is staged on turnIndex (aimock's count of assistant messages; +2 per tool round-trip, +1 per text answer). The highest turnIndex <= assistantCount wins, so each leg carries every absolute position a test reaches it from: a fresh thread (0/2...) AND its slot in the probe's single-thread sequence.

fixtures._comment: tone:professional: turn 1 of d5-agent-config.ts and a fresh thread alike. The probe runs all six prompts in ONE thread, and each turn is a get_app_context read (the adapter's silent built-in; the probe sets the dropdown before sending) plus the answer, 3 assistant messages, so turn k sits at 3k/3k+2. Every later prompt also carries fresh-thread legs at 0/2. The two texts of a pair must differ; responseLength:detailed must be >= 80 chars longer than concise.

response.content: Agent context is a per-turn data bag passed from the frontend to the agent via the useAgentContext hook. On the React side, you call useAgentContext({ description, value }) and CopilotKit sends those values with every run as RunAgentInput.context. This agent reads them at the start of each turn through its get_app_context tool, so every reply reflects the latest frontend state. This enables real-time personalisation: switching a dropdown from 'professional' to 'casual' immediately changes how the agent responds, without restarting the conversation or reconfiguring the backend. The pattern extends to any key-value pair your app needs — feature flags, user roles, locale, or custom metadata.
